headline: Africa: Nigeria: Scores Killed As Military Airstrikes Hit Terrorists in Zamfara
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- Africa: Nigeria: Scores Killed As Military Airstrikes Hit Terrorists in Zamfara.
- South Asia: China says Xi, Trump, Putin to discuss ‘world peace’ in trilateral summit.
- Western Russia: Sixth blackout in two weeks: Russia leaves almost half of Dnipro without power.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Destroyers USS Spruance, USS Michael Murphy return from extended combat deployments.
- Military Times, 9 hours ago: Destroyers USS Spruance, USS Michael Murphy return from extended combat deployments.
The Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyers USS Spruance and USS Michael Murphy returned to their homeports after lengthy deployments during the Iran war.
The Caribbean - bottom line: JAMAICA FIRST.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 21 hours ago: JAMAICA FIRST.
Pushing a Jamaica-first narrative, Jamaica Labour Party (JLP) leader Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness says the country will choose its own path, rejecting foreign blocs, conflicts and dogma amid sustained debate over its foreign policy towards Cuba.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America - bottom line: JP Morgan forecasts 2% monthly inflation in Argentina in 2027.
- Buenos Aires Herald, 13 hours ago: JP Morgan forecasts 2% monthly inflation in Argentina in 2027.
The bank expects 31% annual inflation for 2026, barely below last year's figure, and warns currency pressures could push prices La entrada JP Morgan forecasts 2% monthly inflation in Argentina in 2027 se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Sixth blackout in two weeks: Russia leaves almost half of Dnipro without power.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 9 hours ago: Sixth blackout in two weeks: Russia leaves almost half of Dnipro without power.
Two people have been killed and eight others injured in Russian attacks on Dnipro. The strikes have damaged homes, businesses, vehicles and railway equipment across the city.
- Ukrainska Pravda, The Moscow Times, 11 hours ago: Nuclear safety regulators warn of rising accident risk in Ukraine – Reuters.
Nuclear safety regulators from 38 countries have warned of the increasing threat to Ukrainian nuclear power plants caused by Moscow's strikes on the country's energy system.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 8 hours ago: Zelenskyy warns that Russia is preparing new missile attack.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has warned that Russia may launch a large-scale missile attack on the night of 16-17 November.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 8 hours ago: Komyshuvakha search operation completed: Russian attack killed 72 people – photos.
Two weeks of search operations after Russian guided bombs hit a humanitarian hub on 2 November have ended. Four people are still missing.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Brexit diminished us, Burnham says as he tees up closer EU ties.
- Politico Europe, 4 hours ago: Brexit diminished us, Burnham says as he tees up closer EU ties.
The British prime minister said Brexit was "the first domino to fall in a global move towards isolationism and protectionism."
- Politico Europe, 11 hours ago: Google says Russian speakers pulled off first-ever fully automated AI cyberattack.
The development could mark an inflection point in the use of AI for cyberattacks.
- Balkan Insight, 15 hours ago: Second Trial of Kosovo’s Thaci, for Obstructing Justice, Nears End.
Verdict looms on Tuesday in former President Hashim Thaci's second trial at The Hague, in which he is accused of interfering with witnesses in the earlier war-crimes case against him.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Nigeria: Scores Killed As Military Airstrikes Hit Terrorists in Zamfara.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 21 hours ago: Nigeria: Scores Killed As Military Airstrikes Hit Terrorists in Zamfara.
[Daily Trust] Troops of Operation Fansan Yamma have repelled successive attacks by terrorists on two communities in Anka Local Government Area of Zamfara State, while air strikes reportedly killed scores of the assailants.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 9 hours ago: Somalia: Airstrikes Target Al-Shabaab Weapons and Explosives Depots in Somalia's Lower Shabelle.
[Shabelle] Lower Shabelle -- International partners carried out airstrikes targeting locations allegedly used by Al-Shabaab to store weapons and explosives in Leego village in Somalia's Lower Shabelle region, following planned military operations by Somali special forces.
- Africanews, 14 hours ago: 17 killed in two deadly shootings as South Africa battles rising violent crime.
Seventeen people are dead following two separate mass shootings in South Africa. In the first attack, six men and three women, were found shot dead inside a shack near Pretoria.
- Africanews, 19 hours ago: Sudan and Ethiopia trade accusations over armed groups.
Tensions between Sudan and Ethiopia have escalated, with each accusing the other of supporting armed groups that wage war within its borders, undermining efforts to resolve the conflicts that have gripped the two neighboring African countries.
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Yemeni army reports 661 attacks on Houthis as group advances towards Aden.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, one hour ago: Yemeni army reports 661 attacks on Houthis as group advances towards Aden.
Yemen's army reports 173 Houthi fighters killed or wounded as government forces reposition to defend Aden.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, The Hindu - International, 6 hours ago: Sudanese army air attack kills 13 in western Sudan: Rights group.
'Preliminary monitoring' shows women and children killed, homes destroyed in West Kordofan, says Emergency Lawyers.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Rubio condemns Iranian strikes in Bahrain in call with Bahraini counterpart.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani reaffirmed the two countries' long-standing partnership following multiple Iranian strikes on Bahrain.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: ‘No daylight’: Vance denies rift with Trump over Iran war, vows no ‘forever war’.
Vance said Trump is weighing whether to end the conflict or increase military and diplomatic pressure on Tehran, but insists the US will not remain involved indefinitely.
South Africa - bottom line: Zimbabwe: 'Quit Zanu-PF If Disgruntled' - Mutsvangwa Tells VP Chiwenga As Succession Battle Escalates.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 21 hours ago: Zimbabwe: 'Quit Zanu-PF If Disgruntled' - Mutsvangwa Tells VP Chiwenga As Succession Battle Escalates.
[New Zimbabwe] ZANU PF spokesperson Christopher Mutsvangwa has fired a scathing warning at party leaders unhappy with internal direction, saying they are free to walk out if they are aggrieved.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 15 hours ago: Mozambique: Lam Warns of Possible Flight Disruptions Due to Jet Fuel Supply Constraints.
[AIM] Maputo -- The publicly-owned company Air Mozambique (formerly known as Mozambique Airlines, LAM) has warned of possible flight schedule changes as a result of temporary constraints in the supply of aviation fuel (Jet A-1).
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 15 hours ago: Malawi: Maranatha Boss Urges Students to Challenge Questionable Maneb Results.
[Nyasa Times] The head of Maranatha Academy has warned that many students could be missing out on better examination grades because of widespread misconceptions about the remarking process.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 15 hours ago: Malawi: Chithyola Urges Action On Forex, Fuel, Food and Fertiliser.
[Nyasa Times] Leader of the Opposition and former Finance Minister Simplex Chithyola Banda has urged the government to focus on what he calls the crucial "4Fs" - forex, fuel, food and fertiliser - warning that Malawi will struggle to overcome its economic woes unless all four are addressed together.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: China says Xi, Trump, Putin to discuss ‘world peace’ in trilateral summit.
- Dawn (Pakistan), The Hindu - International, South China Morning Post - China, one hour ago: China says Xi, Trump, Putin to discuss ‘world peace’ in trilateral summit.
The leaders of China, Russia and the United States will discuss “world peace” when they hold their first trilateral summit in Shenzhen this week, Beijing said on Monday. Presidents Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin are due to meet in the southern Chinese city on Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit. China has provided few details as to what the three leaders will discuss but said they would hold “in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations”.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 10 hours ago: Dar says Pakistan to host next Makkah alliance summit later this month.
Pakistan will host the next meeting of the Makkah Defence Alliance’s apex committee, likely later this month, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said on Monday. He made the remarks while answering a query during a press briefing regarding a ministerial meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) held in Islamabad. Asked about regional security architecture, Dar recalled the Aug 7 signing of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. The pact empowers the three states to treat an attack on any one of them as an attack on all.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: At ECO moot, Dar calls for translating 'collective commitments into concrete action'.
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar closed out the 30th meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) Council of Ministers (COM) in Islamabad on Monday with a call for countries to translate their commitments into action. Pakistan, which holds the ECO chairmanship for 2026-27, hosted the meeting under the theme “Reviving Regionalism for a Resilient ECO”. The deputy premier, who chaired the meeting, expressed his “sincere appreciation to all delegations” for their constructive engagement during the meeting.
- The Hindu - International, 3 hours ago: News Analysis | Drone warfare leaves no safe zones in Sudan.
Unmanned strikes are reshaping warfare, disrupting supply lines and expanding the battlefield into previously secure areas. Markets, hospitals, transport hubs, and homes are increasingly targeted, heightening civilian risk amid a deepening humanitarian crisis

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said ⁠on Monday that his nation had ⁠held new online talks with ⁠US presidential envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, as well as European representatives, on the prospects of ending the war with Russia. Zelensky, speaking in his nightly video address, also said Ukraine had intelligence that Russia was ‌planning major strikes on Ukrainian targets on Monday evening, overnight and on Tuesday. The talks came less than a week after US, Ukrainian and Russian...
- South China Morning Post - China, 5 hours ago: Why China is betting on ‘home-court diplomacy’ at the Shenzhen Apec gathering.
In October 2001, with the world still reeling from the September 11 attacks and China on the cusp of joining the World Trade Organization, then Chinese president Jiang Zemin opened the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) leaders’ meeting in Shanghai. The world, he said, was at “a crucial moment, a moment of great hope as well as imposing challenges”. The summit was both a diplomatic debut and a strategic warm-up for China, marking its first major multilateral gathering of this scale. The...

Thousands of customers reported difficulty accessing online accounts at several major US banks and the money transfer service Zelle on Monday after a technical issue at JPMorgan Chase caused ripple effects throughout the financial system. However, Chase said Monday that the technical problems were not the result of a cyberattack, and that it was working to bring banking services back online by the end of the day Monday. “JPMorgan Chase has experienced a temporary issue related to a software bug...
India - bottom line: Iran planning dirty bomb attack in Washington, US intel warns.
- Times of India - Top Stories, Jerusalem Post, just now: Iran planning dirty bomb attack in Washington, US intel warns.
US intelligence indicates that Iran is potentially orchestrating attacks against senior officials, possibly utilizing dirty bombs or chemical weapons. Despite heightened contingency preparations from American authorities, no immediate credible threat has been pinpointed. Additionally, concerns have emerged regarding the likelihood of these weapons being targeted towards US military personnel in the Middle East, although officials question Iran's ability to implement such plans successfully.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: Terror suspect in CRPF attack case killed in Kulgam, 1 flees.
Wanted terrorist Mohammad Latief Bhat managed to escape an extended security cordon, while his aide Umar Nasir was killed.
- NDTV - Top Stories, one hour ago: Tanker Transiting Strait Of Hormuz Attacked Near Oman.
The Iran Navy said the tanker was travelling in a restricted area with its navigation switched off.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 10 hours ago: Nukes, Iran, Ukraine and trade: Trump lays out agenda for trilateral with Xi, Putin.
On November 19, a pivotal trilateral summit will take place in Shenzhen, bringing together leaders from the United States, China, and Russia. Key topics will encompass denuclearisation, the troubling Iran conflict, and the ongoing crisis in Ukraine. Economic discussions will be crucial, focusing on tariffs and tech disputes. Additionally, the strengthening ties between China, Russia, and Iran will be scrutinized amid growing regional tensions.
Korean Peninsula - bottom line: Rubio says Kim Jong Un wants nukes for regime survival, not to support invasions.
- NK News, 20 hours ago: Rubio says Kim Jong Un wants nukes for regime survival, not to support invasions.
North Korea’s nuclear ambitions should be viewed differently from Iran because leader Kim Jong Un seeks regime survival rather than territorial expansion, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said. AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: MP Helen Haines’s first words since leaving hospital after alleged attack led to double amputation.
- The Guardian - Australia, 22 hours ago: MP Helen Haines’s first words since leaving hospital after alleged attack led to double amputation.
Independent MP says she is ‘overwhelmed’ by thousands of warm wishes and thanks Australians for charity donations Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast The independent Australian MP Helen Haines has been discharged from hospital, four weeks after she was allegedly attacked by a man outside her electorate office in Victoria resulting in the amputation of both her legs. In a statement, Haines said she had moved to the rehabilitation stage of her recovery, which would continue in Melbourne. Continue reading...
- The Guardian - Australia, one hour ago: Rio Tinto agrees to pay US$250m to begin repairing ‘devastation’ left by Panguna mine.
Community leader says fund gives chance to find solutions to ‘huge problems we have been living with since the days of the mine’s operation’ Anglo-Australian miner Rio Tinto has agreed to pay a quarter-of-a-billion dollars to begin the clean-up of the toxic Panguna mine site it abandoned more than three decades ago. Panguna, once one of the world’s most profitable gold and copper mines, was shuttered in 1989 after violent protests over environmental damage and the inequitable division of the mine’s profits sparked a decade-long civil war on the Papua New Guinean island of Bougainville.
